  In \eqref{weak_form} the boundary condition has been defined using the Gaussian beam profile 
  \eqref{gaussian_beam_3d} for the sake of simplicity. If specific values are available for the 
  incoming wave, e.g., as provided by an experiment or a separate numerical solver, these values
  could be used as well to define the boundary source term $\boldsymbol{s}^\mathrm{inc}$.

title: Remark
body_md:
The long-time stability result shown for the Poisson splitting scheme in \eqref{long_time_stability_coeffs_Poisson} does not imply that $\boldsymbol{R}$ decreases in time.
 The analysis shows that under certain assumptions, we can construct a time-harmonic solution $\boldsymbol{U}_h^\mathrm{th}$ such that $ \| \boldsymbol{U}_h(t^n) - \boldsymbol{U}_h^\mathrm{th}(t^n)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ cannot increase as $n$ increases. Here $\boldsymbol{U}_h^\mathrm{th}$ is a solution of the time-domain problem \eqref{weak_form} and not the frequency-domain problem \eqref{weak_form_freq_pb}. In fact, we note that the coefficients of $\boldsymbol{U}_h^\mathrm{th}$ given in \eqref{coeffs_timeharmonic_Poisson} depend on $\Delta t$. In other words, the electric field of $\boldsymbol{U}_h^\mathrm{th}$ is an approximation of $\boldsymbol{E}_h^\mathrm{th}$ using the time-evolution problem and therefore it involves the errors related to the time discretization. In contrast, the frequency-domain problem \eqref{semidiscrete_freqdomain} does not involve the time discretization and therefore it provides a more reliable reference solution.



 In fact, there are certain reasons to suspect that in practice $\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty} \|\boldsymbol{R}\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \neq 0$. Firstly, the source spectrum in the time-domain and frequency-domain problem is not the same. The time-domain problem has an initialization, which introduces high frequencies in the spectrum. Besides, the envelope for the Gaussian beam given in \eqref{gaussian_beam_envelope} introduces certain artificial frequencies in the first time-steps. Unless the corresponding modes are part of the transient regime and propagate outwards through the boundary $\Gamma_A$, they inevitably contribute to $\boldsymbol{R}$.
 A secondary factor that may influence the convergence of $\boldsymbol{R}$ is that, contrary to the numerical solution, $\boldsymbol{E}_h^\mathrm{th}$ is not affected by the time-splitting error.
 \label{remark_conv_timeharmonic}
